sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.

sentence: I downloaded ___ MP3 file from the band's website.
explanation: 'MP3' is pronounced /em/, a vowel sound, so 'an'.

sentence: He was born in ___ Netherlands, not in Belgium.
explanation: Country names that are plural or contain 'Kingdom/Republic/States' take 'the': the Netherlands.

sentence: ___ sun sets much later in summer.
explanation: 'The sun' — there is only one, so the definite article is used.

sentence: I saw ___ film last night, and the film was about mountain climbers.
hint: first mention of one of many
explanation: First mention of a countable noun takes 'a'; the second mention becomes 'the' (already written out here).

sentence: They sailed across ___ Mediterranean last summer.
explanation: Seas and oceans take 'the': the Mediterranean.

sentence: ___ Alps attract skiers from all over the world.
explanation: Mountain ranges take 'the' (the Alps), but single peaks take no article (Everest).

sentence: Mount Everest is ___ highest mountain in the world.
explanation: Superlatives take 'the': the highest.

sentence: She was elected ___ president of the students' union.
explanation: After 'elect/appoint/make + role', the article is usually dropped: elected president.

sentence: ___ rich should do more to help the poor.
explanation: The + adjective = a group of people: the rich.

sentence: She goes to ___ school by bus every morning.
explanation: 'Go to school/work/bed/church' (as participant) takes no article.

sentence: I live on ___ Baker Street, near the tube station.
explanation: Street names take no article: Baker Street, Oxford Street.

sentence: ___ United Kingdom consists of four countries.
explanation: 'The United Kingdom', 'the USA', 'the Czech Republic' all take 'the'.

sentence: We visited ___ Louvre on our last morning in Paris.
explanation: Most famous buildings and monuments take 'the': the Louvre, the Eiffel Tower.

sentence: These apples cost two euros ___ kilo.
explanation: 'A/per' is used for rates: two euros a kilo, twice a week, 60 km an hour.

sentence: She goes to the gym twice ___ week.
explanation: 'Twice a week' — rates take 'a' (= per). The other gap is 'the gym'.

sentence: She's got ___ few friends in Madrid, so she visits often.
explanation: 'A few' means some (positive); 'few' alone means hardly any.

sentence: There was ___ enormous queue for the tickets.
explanation: 'Enormous' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an enormous queue'.

sentence: ___ honesty is the best policy, as the saying goes.
explanation: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article: honesty, happiness, love.

sentence: The car crashed into a wall at ___ speed of 90 km/h.
explanation: 'At a speed of…' — 'a' is part of this fixed phrase.

sentence: We stayed at ___ hotel right next to the station.
explanation: 'The station' — in a town there is usually one known station; context makes it definite.

sentence: ___ problem is that people don't recycle enough.
explanation: The problem (the one we are discussing); people in general takes no article.

sentence: She works as ___ waitress during the summer holidays.
explanation: After 'as' and 'work as', jobs take a/an: work as a waitress.

sentence: ___ Everest was first climbed in 1953.
explanation: Single mountain peaks take no article: Everest, Mont Blanc (compare: the Alps).

sentence: He was sent to ___ prison for armed robbery.
explanation: 'Be sent to prison' (as a prisoner) takes no article; visiting the building is 'go to the prison'.

sentence: His wife goes to ___ prison every Sunday to visit him.
explanation: Here 'the prison' is the building she visits, not the institution of imprisonment.

sentence: It was such ___ awful weather that we stayed indoors.
explanation: Uncountable nouns take no article after 'such': such awful weather.

sentence: He had ___ operation on his knee last year.
explanation: 'Operation' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an operation'.

sentence: ___ life in the countryside is much quieter.
explanation: 'Life' in a general sense takes no article: Life is hard sometimes.

sentence: The novel had a huge effect on ___ young people of the 1960s.
explanation: 'The young people of the 1960s' — defined by the of-phrase, so 'the'.

sentence: He earns fifty thousand pounds ___ year.
explanation: 'Fifty thousand a year' — 'a' = per in rates.

sentence: My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.

sentence: Do you know ___ Smiths who live opposite?
explanation: 'The + plural surname' = the family: the Smiths.

sentence: ___ inflation rose sharply last quarter.
explanation: 'Inflation' as a general economic concept takes no article.

sentence: He was ___ last person to leave the building.
explanation: Ordinals take 'the': the last person, the first time.

sentence: We go to ___ cinema about once a month.
explanation: 'Go to the cinema/theatre' is a fixed phrase with 'the'.

sentence: She was wearing ___ old denim jacket that I loved at first sight.
explanation: 'An old…' — 'old' starts with a vowel sound.

sentence: ___ unemployment has fallen sharply this year.
explanation: Unemployment as a general concept takes no article.

sentence: They organized ___ charity concert for flood victims.
explanation: 'A charity concert' — one of many possible concerts, first mention.

sentence: ___ water in this bottle tastes strange.
explanation: The of/in-phrase makes the noun definite: the water in this bottle.

sentence: He considers himself ___ expert on medieval art.
explanation: 'An expert' — 'expert' starts with a vowel sound.

sentence: Could you pass me ___ salt, please?
explanation: 'The salt' — both speakers know which one (on the table).

sentence: She gets up at six and watches ___ morning news.
explanation: 'The morning news' — a specific known broadcast, so 'the'.

sentence: It was ___ best meal I've ever had.
explanation: Superlatives take 'the': the best meal.

sentence: Rome is ___ capital of Italy.
explanation: 'The capital of Italy' — the of-phrase makes it unique and definite.

sentence: He was offered ___ job in the human resources department.
explanation: 'A job' — first mention of one of many possible jobs. Note: 'in human resources' takes no article.

sentence: ___ courage he showed amazed everyone.
explanation: 'The courage he showed' — the relative clause makes it definite.

sentence: We had ___ wonderful time in Prague.
explanation: 'Have a wonderful/great/good time' — 'time' here is countable and takes 'a'.

sentence: ___ influenza, or flu, is highly contagious.
explanation: Most disease names take no article: influenza, flu, malaria (compare: the flu is also heard informally).

sentence: She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

sentence: ___ noise woke me up in the middle of the night.
explanation: 'The noise' — the one that woke me; 'in the night' is a fixed phrase.

sentence: She put ___ money in the safe before leaving.
explanation: 'The money' and 'the safe' are specific in the situation.

sentence: He is ___ most experienced teacher in the school.
explanation: Superlative + of/in-phrase: the most experienced teacher in the school.

sentence: I'd like ___ orange juice, please — small or large?
explanation: Drinks offered as an amount take 'some' (or no article): some orange juice.

sentence: ___ poverty remains a serious issue worldwide.
explanation: 'Poverty' in general takes no article.

sentence: He joined ___ army when he was eighteen.
explanation: Institutions take 'the': the army, the police, the church.

sentence: The tour included ___ visit to the British Museum.
explanation: 'A visit' (one of many possible) and 'the British Museum' (museums take 'the').

sentence: She made ___ decision to move to the countryside.
explanation: 'Make a decision' is the fixed collocation; 'the countryside' is a fixed phrase with 'the'.

sentence: ___ books you left on my desk were really useful.
explanation: 'The books you left…' — the clause identifies which books.

sentence: He left ___ school at sixteen and went straight into a job.
explanation: Leave school (finish education) takes no article.

sentence: It's ___ pity that the concert was cancelled.
explanation: 'It's a pity' is a fixed expression with 'a'.

sentence: ___ young woman at reception speaks five languages.
explanation: 'The young woman at reception' — defined by the location phrase.

sentence: This is ___ second time you've been late this week.
explanation: 'The second time' — ordinals take 'the'.

sentence: They drove to ___ south of France for the summer.
explanation: 'By train' takes no article; 'the south of France' takes 'the' (compass areas).

sentence: He's always been fascinated by ___ universe.
explanation: 'The universe' — unique, so 'the'.

sentence: We bought ___ antique mirror at the flea market.
explanation: 'An antique mirror' — 'antique' starts with a vowel sound.

sentence: ___ information you sent was extremely helpful.
explanation: 'The information you sent' — the clause defines it; information is uncountable.

sentence: She earns her living as ___ journalist.
explanation: Jobs after 'as' take a/an: as a journalist.

sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).

sentence: They say ___ apple a day keeps the doctor away.
explanation: 'An apple a day…' — 'an' before the vowel sound, 'a' before 'day'.

sentence: ___ Galapagos Islands are famous for unique wildlife.
explanation: Groups of islands take 'the': the Galapagos Islands, the Canary Islands.

sentence: He's got ___ MA in translation.
explanation: 'MA' is pronounced /em/, starting with a vowel sound, so 'an MA'.

sentence: We reached ___ agreement after hours of negotiation.
explanation: 'Reach an agreement' — 'agreement' starts with a vowel sound.

sentence: ___ happiness matters more than money.
explanation: Both 'happiness' and 'money' are general here, so no article for either gap.

sentence: She works in ___ insurance, not banking.
explanation: Industry/sector names take no article: in insurance, in banking, in marketing.

sentence: The kids spent ___ afternoon playing in the garden.
explanation: 'The afternoon' and 'the garden' (our garden) are definite in context.

sentence: He demands ___ answer before the end of the day.
explanation: An answer — vowel sound.

sentence: ___ spaceship travelled for six months before reaching Mars.
explanation: The spaceship — the one in the story; Mars takes no article.

sentence: He behaves as if he were ___ owner of the company.
explanation: 'The owner' — there is one owner, so 'the'.

sentence: I only need ___ few more minutes to finish.
explanation: 'A few minutes' = some minutes; 'few' alone would mean almost none.

sentence: ___ curiosity killed the cat, as they say.
explanation: 'Curiosity' as an abstract quality takes no article, even in the proverb.

sentence: She's studying history at ___ University of Vienna.
explanation: University names with of-phrases take the: the University of Vienna.

sentence: He gave me ___ useful advice about the paperwork.
explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — never 'an advice'. Use 'a piece of advice' for one item.

sentence: They moved to ___ coastal town an hour south of the capital.
explanation: A coastal town — first mention of one of many.

sentence: ___ weather was so bad that the match was abandoned.
explanation: The weather is always definite in a situation.

sentence: It's ___ eight o'clock news — hurry up!
explanation: 'The eight o'clock news' — a specific, known programme.

sentence: He was wearing ___ strange metal bracelet on his left wrist.
explanation: 'A strange bracelet' (first mention); body parts after prepositions traditionally take 'the' (on the left wrist).

sentence: ___ good news is that sales are up by twenty per cent.
explanation: 'News' is uncountable but takes 'the' when specified: the good news is… 'Sales' here is general, so no article.

sentence: She got ___ injury during the warm-up.
explanation: 'An injury' — vowel sound; 'during the warm-up' is the specific one.

sentence: ___ rich variety of birds lives in the Danube delta.
explanation: A rich variety of… — variety is countable here, first mention.

sentence: He drives ___ old van that is always breaking down.
explanation: 'An old van' — 'old' begins with a vowel sound. The second gap is 'the axle'.

sentence: They're building ___ new library near the town hall.
explanation: A new library — first mention; the town hall is the known one.

sentence: ___ antibiotics don't help against flu.
explanation: Plural general nouns and flu (illness name) take no article.

sentence: It was ___ honour to meet the ambassador.
explanation: 'Honour' starts with a vowel sound (silent h), so 'an honour'.

sentence: He ordered ___ steak, but it arrived cold.
explanation: 'A steak' first, then 'the waiter' — the restaurant's waiter, definite in context.

sentence: ___ sales figures for October look promising.
explanation: 'The sales figures for October' — defined by the for-phrase.

sentence: She has ___ eye for detail.
explanation: 'Have an eye for something' — fixed idiom with 'an'.

sentence: ___ French enjoy good food.
explanation: 'The + nationality adjective' = the people as a group: the French, the British.

sentence: He found ___ coin buried in the sand.
explanation: 'A coin' first mention; 'in the sand' — sand as a mass takes 'the' here (the sand on that beach).

sentence: They elected her ___ chairperson for a second term.
explanation: After 'elect/appoint', roles take no article: elected her chairperson.

sentence: ___ noise pollution in cities is getting worse.
explanation: 'Noise pollution' as a general concept takes no article.

sentence: We're going to ___ Algarve for a fortnight in June.
explanation: Region names often take the: the Algarve, the Riviera.
